beats.intent: ThinkSR keeps a dense carrier while a compact DQ-CTM process repeatedly reads and updates it before decoding.
beats.claim: ThinkSR end to end: encoder, windows, shared DQ-CTM ticks, decoder.
beats.narration: The method is built around a dense carrier that survives through the compact thought process. The encoder turns the low-resolution input into that carrier field. Windowing presents the field in local token groups without dropping the spatial structure. The DQ-CTM thought process ticks recurrently, with parameters shared across those ticks. The decoder turns the updated dense representation back into the super-resolved image.

beats.intent: The carrier equation first makes a dense feature field from the low-resolution image, then partitions that field into tokens.
beats.narration: The carrier starts as a dense feature field, not as a compact state. The encoder maps the low-resolution image into that field. The window partition operates on the field and keeps every token for the thought process.
